questions.question: What is a primary strategic benefit of adopting an open innovation model regarding intellectual property? a). It eliminates the need for internal R&D entirely. b). It allows companies to maintain absolute secrecy over all their technological developments. c). It facilitates shared R&D risks and reduces time to market through IP collaboration. d). It guarantees that a company will never face patent infringement lawsuits. / [CO4] [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html: • c) It facilitates shared R&D risks and reduces time to market through IP collaboration.

questions.question: Discuss the importance of related rights and whom they protect. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Related rights protect performers, producers of sound recordings, and broadcasting
  • organizations-they are crucial for safeguarding creative contributions that are not covered
  • under traditional copyright -these rights ensure fair remuneration and control over the use of
  • performances, recordings, and broadcasts.

questions.question: Discuss on WIPO. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• World Intellectual Property Organization- promotes global IPR protection and cooperation
  • - established in 1967 and headquartered in Geneva - administers international treaties and
  • registration systems - encourages innovation creativity and technology transfer among member
  • countries.

questions.question: Write on the rights of the Copyright holder in Literary, Dramatic and Musical works / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Copyright holders of literary, dramatic, and musical works have exclusive rights to
  • reproduce, publish, perform, adapt, and communicate their works to the public -these rights
  • help maintain control over creative output and enable the creator to earn recognition and
  • financial benefit.

questions.question: Discuss on Patents. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Patents provide exclusive legal rights to inventors for new inventions - protection usually
  • lasts for twenty years from filing date - prevents unauthorized making using or selling of
  • invention - encourages research development and technological advancement in industries.

questions.question: Compare and contrast the protection offered by patents and industrial designs. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Patents protect inventions that are novel and useful, while industrial designs protect the
  • aesthetic or ornamental aspects of a product-Patents offer broader technical protection, whereas
  • design rights focus on visual appearance. Both stimulate innovation but serve different creative
  • outcomes.

questions.question: Mention any three works that. are protected under copyright law. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Literary works such as books and articles are protected under copyright law - musical works
  • and artistic creations also receive protection - cinematograph films computer software and
  • sound recordings are covered - safeguards creators against unauthorized c opying and
  • distribution.

questions.question: Discuss the role of intellectual property rights in fostering economic growth. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Intellectual property rights encourage innovation by granting legal protection to creators
  • and inventors-this boosts investment, job creation, and competitive advantage-IPR also attracts
  • foreign direct investment and boosts research and development, thus contributing significantly
  • to economic development.

questions.question: Explain how Intellectual Property Rights protection encourages innovative activities. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Intellectual Property Rights - provide legal protection for inventions and creative works -
  • encourages inventors and creators to invest in research and innovation - ensures economic
  • rewards and market advantage - promotes technological progress industrial growth and healthy
  • competition.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of Indian courts in shaping IPR jurisprudence with the help of landmark judgments. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Indian courts have played a crucial role in interpreting and enforcing IPR laws. Landmark
  • cases like Novartis v. Union of India and Yahoo Inc. v. Akash Arora helped define patentability
  • and trademark infringement, shaping a balanced approach to innovation and public interest.

questions.question: Briefly explain India’s obligations under the TRIPS Agreement. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• India under TRIPS Agreement must provide minimum standards of IPR protection -
  • required to amend patent copyright and trademark laws according to WTO norms - ensures
  • enforcement mechanisms against infringement - balances public interest with protection of
  • innovation and trade.

questions.question: Discuss the benefits and risks of adopting open innovation in R&D- heavy industries such as pharmaceuticals or software. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Open innovation enables knowledge sharing and speeds up product development, reducing
  • R&D costs-however, it also risks intellectual property leakage, loss of competitive advantage,
  • and coordination challenges -Industries like pharmaceuticals and software must balance
  • openness with protective measures for sustainable innovation.

questions.question: Define compulsory licensing. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Compulsory licensing- allows government to authorize use of patented invention without
  • patent holder’s consent - granted under special conditions like public health emergencies or
  • non-availability of product - ensures wider access to essential goods especially medicines.

questions.question: Explain the concept of Copyleft licensing. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Copyleft licensing allows users to freely use, modify, and distribute software or content,
  • provided derivative works carry the same license -promotes collaboration and transparency
  • while preventing proprietary control over modified versions, commonly used in open -source
  • communities like Linux or GNU.

questions.question: Can an Artificial Intelligence system be legally recognized as the "inventor" on a patent? Briefly explain the current legal consensus. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Present legal systems - generally do not recognize Artificial Intelligence as an inventor -
  • patent laws in most countries require inventor to be a natural person - AI can assist innovation
  • processes but ownership and inventorship are assigned to humans.

questions.question: What is the objective of the Trade Marks Act, 1999 in India? / [CO4] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• The Trade Marks Act, 1999 aims to protect trademarks for goods and services, prevent
  • misuse or duplication, and ensure fair trade practices -grants exclusive rights to brand owners
  • and helps consumers identify product origin, supporting brand reputation and market integrity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Design Act, 2000 in India? / [CO4] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Design Act 2000 in India- protects the visual appearance and aesthetic features of products
  • - covers shape configuration pattern and ornamentation of industrial designs - prevents
  • unauthorized copying of registered designs - promotes creativity and commercial
  • competitiveness in industries.

questions.question: Discuss on the emergence of WTO / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) emerged in 1995 as a successor to GATT to regulate
  • international trade-provides a framework for negotiating trade agreements, resolving disputes,
  • and ensuring fair competition-WTO plays a key role in promoting globalization, reducing trade
  • barriers, and enforcing intellectual property standards globally.

questions.question: How did GATT influence international Trade policies? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade- promoted reduction of tariffs and trade barriers
  • among nations - encouraged free and fair international trade through multilateral negotiations
  • and trade agreements - established rules for resolving trade disputes and preventing
  • discrimination - contributed to expansion of global markets economic cooperation and
  • international trade liberalization - later evolved into the World Trade Organization in 1995.

questions.question: Explain how IPR can attract foreign direct investment and promote entrepreneurship. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) offer legal protection to innovations, making markets
  • more secure and attractive for foreign investors -strong IPR regimes encourage technology
  • transfer, joint ventures, and R&D-for entrepreneurs, IPR enables monetization of ideas, builds
  • brand value, and fosters a competitive business environment, driving economic and innovation-
  • led growth.

questions.question: Analyze how Indian laws align with the TRIPS Agreement. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Indian IPR laws, including the Patents Act, Trademarks Act, and Copyright Act, have been
  • amended to comply with TRIPS -they balance innovation incentives with public interest by
  • ensuring patentability standards, compulsory licensing provisions, and data protection, thus
  • aligning domestic regulations with global intellectual property norms.

questions.question: Discuss the core principles of open-source software licensing. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Open-source software licensing- allows users to freely use modify and distribute software
  • - promotes transparency collaboration and community driven innovation among developers
  • worldwide - source code remains accessible encouraging improvement and error correction by
  • users - licenses such as GPL and MIT ensure legal rights and responsibilities - reduces software
  • costs and supports technological advancement and digital accessibility.

questions.question: Write the importance of PCT. / [CO1] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• The Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) simplifies the international patent application process
  • by allowing inventors to seek protection in multiple countries through a single application -
  • reduces administrative burden, provides more time for market evaluation, and promotes global
  • innovation by streamlining the procedure for acquiring patent rights internationally

questions.question: Discuss the ongoing challenges posed by digital piracy in the modern era of the internet. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Digital piracy- involves unauthorized copying downloading and distribution of copyrighted
  • content through the internet - causes major financial losses to software , music, film and
  • publishing industries worldwide - rapid technological advancement and online file sharing
  • platforms make enforcement difficult - piracy weakens incentives for creators and innovators
  • - governments and companies use stricter cyber laws digital rights management and awareness
  • campaigns to combat piracy.
